data.name: Aloysius
data.gender_notes: Aloysius is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Roman name Aloysius, meaning 'famed warrior', 'noble', or 'handsome'. In Christianity, St. Aloysius is a Jesuit saint known for his strong spiritual devotion, loyalty to the Catholic Church, and heroic life. The name Aloysius carries the meaning “Famed warrior” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Aloysius usually hope their child will grow to embody famed warrior and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aloysius total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Aloysius is of ancient Roman origin and has been used throughout history. It carries connotations of strength, nobility, and martial prowess. Aloysius has been a popular name in various cultures, including Italian, French, and English, and has been borne by numerous historical figures and fictional characters.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, St. Aloysius is revered for his deep spirituality, piety, and commitment to the Catholic faith. Born into a noble family in Italy in 1582, Aloysius demonstrated a remarkable spiritual sensitivity from a young age. Despite his privileged upbringing, he chose to embrace a life of poverty and devotion, joining the Society of Jesus (the Jesuits) at the age of 18. Throughout his life, St. Aloysius was renowned for his extensive prayer life, his charitable works, and his remarkable wisdom beyond his years. He died at the age of 23, after a short but heroic battle with illness. St. Aloysius' legacy as a model of Christian virtue and devotion continues to inspire many to this day.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Aloysius derives from the Latin name 'Aloisus', meaning 'famous or noble' in the sense of 'noble with God'. This name was particularly revered in the Middle Ages for those who chose a life of devotion and piety.
